answer: Each identity claims one tundra plot, locks an 80-credit bond, and posts one dawn prism reading per epoch: the prism splits dawn light off the plot, and its spectrum, serial and key go on the tundra board. Auditors recompute albedo from spectrum and dawn angle; a mismatch over 3%, a reused serial, or a copied spectrum burns the bond. The first plot costs 36 credits, the kth 36+7(k-1), so 1000 fakes cost 3,532,500 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-prism ring fails: one prism cannot match two serials at different dawn angles. An honest plot pays 36 once, bond redeemed after a clean epoch.
